svg.title: Job expansion: the loop in Plan()
svg.desc: Three pending jobs go through the switch in Plan(). Successful jobs get the next job_index; a failed job is reported immediately and does not consume an index.

g.text: jN = job index; only the rule-B chain is drawn

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Plan() does not remove events if a job method fails after it has already appended some (for example a VecsTransition or a bay transition before a later check fails). Those events keep the failed job's index,

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: which the next successful job then reuses. The job methods above fail before adding anything, so this example is clean; the 'Gotchas' subsection of section 12 lists where it can happen.

g.text: Job expansion: the loop in Plan()

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Plan() walks request.pending_jobs in order and switches on job.type. Each successful job is appended to plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs, so job_index (= its position there) is only counted for
